title: Concord adapter: ergonomic bridge for AsyncIterator ↔ WebStream in TS SDK
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a new TypeScript SDK adapter (internal name: Concord) that provides a first-class ergonomic bridge between AsyncIterator-based consumers/producers and WHATWG ReadableStream / Node/DOM Web Streams. Goals: 1) eliminate common footguns for SDK users when consuming streaming LLM outputs across Node/Deno/Browser; 2) preserve backpressure semantics and deterministic cancellation propagation; 3) provide easy-to-use examples and utility helpers for resume/retry and framing; 4) keep the public surface minimal and documented for v2.5.0.
acceptance_criteria: Concord API exposed as SDK utility (concordBridge) with documented types and examples in README
Interop tests pass: Node (ReadableStream), Browser (ReadableStream), Deno (ReadableStream), and AsyncIterator consumers all consume the same stream identity without data duplication
Cancellation propagates: AbortSignal passed into producer ends iteration and closes underlying stream; no orphaned promises or memory leaks in stress tests
Backpressure preserved: producer does not outpace consumer under slow consumer scenario (validated via benchmark harness)
Resume semantics: when retry policy triggers, the adapter supports safe replay of prefix buffer up to configured max without violating ordering
Performance: added overhead <5% median token latency in microbench vs current bridge shim under typical payloads
Type definitions ship and compile with strict TypeScript settings in downstream clients
Examples: at least three canonical examples (browser fetch -> async iterator, Node SDK streaming -> WebStream pipeTo, duplex bidi example) included in examples/ and docs site
design_decisions: Expose a single top-level helper: concordBridge(source, options) -> { asyncIterator, readableStream } to let callers pick their preferred consumer without forcing conversion apis
Adopt AbortSignal as the canonical cancellation primitive across environments; polyfill warnings for older runtimes are surfaced in README
Internal buffering limited to a configurable small window (default 32 chunks) to enable safe retry/resume but limit memory usage
Do not attempt to fully unify Node streams2/3 APIs; scope to WHATWG ReadableStream and AsyncIterator for now to reduce surface area
Retry/resume is implemented as a shallow prefix cache with explicit hooks for prompt-level replay; we avoid implicit log-structured replay to prevent surprising semantics
tradeoffs: Keeping the API small simplifies adoption but means some advanced use-cases (e.g., raw TCP-like streaming) are not covered and will continue to require custom glue code
Supporting AbortSignal across all runtimes requires either small runtime shims or conditional code paths; chosen approach increases install-time bundle by ~1kB but keeps runtime complexity low
Providing both AsyncIterator and ReadableStream views duplicates some runtime bookkeeping which increases nominal CPU and memory overhead vs single-view specialized adaptors
Prefix buffer for resume increases memory usage for very long prefix tokens; we mitigate by defaulting to a small window and documenting larger memory implications
implementation_notes: Add new module: packages/sdk/src/concord.ts containing concordBridge implementation and internal helpers
Export types in packages/sdk/src/index.ts and update public API docs and changelog
Implementation will rely on conditional runtime checks: globalThis.ReadableStream presence, isNode check for using stream.Readable.toWeb where available
Core adapter maintains a single source-of-truth queue; when returning both asyncIterator and readableStream views, they reference the same queue and share cancellation signals
Provide small helper: frameDecoder/encoder for chunk framing (useful for token deltas vs metadata events)
Add runtime assertions to detect double-consume attempts and surface helpful error messages linking to docs
test_plan: Unit tests: simulate producer generating 100k small chunks; validate consumer backpressure, order, and cancellation behavior
Integration tests: example-apps/browser-consume and node-consume run in CI using playwright for browser path
Fuzz tests: random pause/resume patterns, abrupt AbortSignal triggers, and intermittent network stalls
Performance bench: microbench harness to compare current shim vs Concord under three load shapes (small-token, long-token, bursty) and report p50/p95 token latency
Leak detection: run long-lived stream producers under heap profiler to ensure no retained closures after cancellation
rollout_plan: Soft-launch in Canary channel: publish ts-sdk-2.5.0-canary with concord behind an opt-in flag (SDK.concord = true) for two weeks
Collect telemetry: add opt-in telemetry events for conversion, cancel, and resume counts (no PII) during canary
Docs & migration: publish docs/guides/concord.md with migration guide from existing bridge-helpers and examples
GA release: flip opt-in flag to default after canary if no regressions and metrics OK; create deprecation RFC for very old bridge helper if applicable
Post-release follow-up: monitor errors/latency dashboards for 2 weeks and schedule quick patch if >5% regressions observed
